Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 16:24:00 -0700
Subject: HealthScope — model fit & safety evals follow-up

Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and next steps from our side:

- Recommended model candidates for your use case (clinical triage + summarization):
  - redwood-guanaco-34b-int8 (best latency/cost balance for medium-length notes)
  - redwood-llama-70b-q4 (higher quality for long-form summarization; consider for batch jobs)

- Deliverables we attached / linked:
  - healthscope-eval-results.csv (initial benchmark on your redacted sample data)
  - safety-prompt-sets.pdf (examples of guardrail prompts and refusal templates)
  - Drive link with full eval dashboard: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1abcDEFgHIJkLmno

- Next steps we propose:
  1) Rafael to run a targeted PHI/refusal eval (sensitive domain prompts) and return flagged examples.
  2) Redwood to share a short MUTUAL ACTION PLAN and a canary deployment plan for a week-long trial on Dedicated capacity.
  3) Quick sync next week to review results and lock an initial pilot scope.

A few notes on safety/guardrails from the call: you mentioned PHI-handling and refusal policy (must not hallucinate diagnoses or reveal identifiers). Rafael and I will scope additional prompt-based tests and a small policy-eval that simulates adversarial prompts.

If that plan looks good, can you confirm the list of sample data we should use for the PHI eval (redacted examples are fine), and availability for a 30-min review next Tue/Wed?

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: HealthScope — model fit & safety evals follow-up

Marissa / Rafael —

Thanks for the clear recap and the materials. A few quick items from our side:

- We can provide 100 de-identified notes (redacted) for the PHI eval but will need to confirm with security on the exact redaction rules. I looped them in (security@healthscope.org).
- Can you confirm whether the model inference path will ever persist raw inputs in any non-ephemeral logs? We require no PHI persistence off our environment.
- On refusal behavior: we need examples showing that the model will refuse to provide a diagnosis or attempt to extract identifiers when prompted adversarially. Could you include a short sample prompt + model response as part of the deliverable?

Also, quick governance ask: do you support pinning models to specific quantized variants (e.g., q4 vs int8) and do we get model provenance metadata for auditing?

Elena
Dr. Elena Martinez
Director, Clinical Informatics | HealthScope
elena.martinez@healthscope.org

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HealthScope — model fit & safety evals follow-up

Elena / Tom / Marissa —

Thanks — Rafael here (inference bench/ops). Wanted to surface the technical approach we'll run and confirm items Elena asked about.

1) Data persistence: Redwood's hosted inference can be configured not to persist raw input tokens. For Dedicated / Private we can ensure no customer data leaves your VPC and logs can be configured to redact inputs. I will include a short data-flow diagram in the M.A.P.

2) Safety/refusal eval: we'll run three tiers:
   a) baseline quality/regression tests (perplexity/ROUGE on the redacted notes)
   b) adversarial refusal tests (prompt-set attached) — we will enumerate prompts that attempt to elicit diagnoses or identifiers and record model responses and confidence heuristics
   c) policy behavior checks (blacklist/whitelist rule triggers + few-shot pattern tests)

I attached a starter set of guardrail prompts and a CSV of initial eval results from your redacted sample. We'll flag any hallucination/PII leakage examples.

Attachments: [healthscope-eval-results.csv], [safety-prompt-sets.pdf]

3) Pinning & provenance: yes — we support pinning to a model artifact (e.g., redwood-llama-70b-q4-v1) and we emit provenance metadata (model id, quantization, kernel/runtime) in the audit logs for each inference. We'll include a sample audit record format in the MAP.

4) Canary plan & timeline: propose a 1-week Dedicated canary with a 10k-token/day cap. We'll run the PHI/refusal tests in parallel and reconvene with results after 7 days. If you'd like, we can prioritize the refusal tests first and run the pilot after acceptance criteria are met.

Proposed action: Elena / security team to approve the redaction rules and send the sample notes. We'll begin the refusal tests as soon as we have the files (SFTP or Secure Drive OK).

-Rafael
Rafael Mendes
